supported_providers.summary: Stripe is the only payment provider XBorderCo integrates with today, and only for integrations that produce a Stripe invoice. XBorderCo applies tax when an invoice is created, so a setup that never creates one cannot be processed.

integration_types.notes: No-code; the payment page lives on buy.stripe.com. Only available to certain Stripe customers. First-subscription caveat: Stripe creates and pays the first invoice atomically, so it cannot be amended — the customer is pointed to XBorderCo's own tax invoice via the invoice footer. Renewals are amended normally.

Also called Stripe Checkout Sessions. Your backend creates the session and redirects the customer to a Stripe-hosted page. Same first-subscription caveat as Payment Links; one-off payments are invoiced by XBorderCo after checkout completes.
Stripe Elements inside your own pages. XBorderCo's preferred integration type — it gives the clearest view of the transaction.
Create invoices with auto_advance: false so the draft is held for XBorderCo to amend, and give customers an address.country.
Set a future billing_cycle_anchor with proration_behavior: 'none' so the first invoice is created as a draft.

unsupported_integration_types.why: No invoice is created, so XBorderCo never sees the transaction and cannot apply or account for tax on it.
unsupported_integration_types.detection_signal: Charges in computed/stripe-setup.json carrying no invoice id.

unsupported_integration_types.why: Stripe finalises the invoice before XBorderCo can amend it — a race condition. The setting has to be off.
unsupported_integration_types.detection_signal: Checkout sessions with invoice_creation.enabled, counted by actions/fetch-checkout-config.ts and reported in computed/stripe-setup.json warnings.

roadmap_providers.notes: Integrations beyond Stripe are on the roadmap. If you use another provider and want to be in touch about future integrations, contact the XBorderCo team.

fit_guidance: Map the merchant's setup to a verdict, and NEVER default to supported. SUPPORTED only if they run Stripe through one of the listed supported integration_types. NOT YET SUPPORTED if their setup appears in unsupported_integration_types — say so plainly; silence here is the costliest error this assessment can make, because it is discovered after they have committed. ROADMAP if they use a non-Stripe provider (their obligations still hold; XBC support is on the roadmap). When the integration type cannot be confirmed, say it is unconfirmed and name what would confirm it — do not assume the supported case. If computed/stripe-setup.json reports charges without invoices, ask the merchant once which integration they use — a missing invoice id is a reason to ask, not evidence of PaymentIntents: one-off Checkout and Payment Link sales carry no invoice and are supported. If they cannot confirm, the verdict is UNCONFIRMED and the report is still delivered in full; integration checks never block the exposure analysis.
